source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.6.5 (Khintchine's inequality), complete displayed inequality and following sentence defining K and C
source_evidence.observation: The exercise assumes independent sub-gaussian random variables X_1,...,X_N with zero means and unit variances, takes a=(a_1,...,a_N) in R^N, and asks for every p in [2,infinity) to prove (sum_i a_i^2)^(1/2) <= ||sum_i a_i X_i||_{L^p} <= C K sqrt(p) (sum_i a_i^2)^(1/2), where K=max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2} and C is absolute.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (2.15) and the sentence immediately following equations (2.14)--(2.16)
source_evidence.observation: Every sub-gaussian random variable X satisfies ||X||_{L^p} <= C ||X||_{psi_2} sqrt(p) for every p>=1; the source states that C is a positive absolute constant and that, up to absolute factors, the psi_2 norm is the smallest scale making the inequality valid.
A random variable satisfying any of properties i--iv of Proposition 2.5.2 is called sub-gaussian, and its sub-gaussian norm is defined by ||X||_{psi_2}=inf{t>0 : E exp(X^2/t^2)<=2}.
The source writes the L^p norm as ||X||_{L^p}=(E|X|^p)^(1/p).

binders: A positive finite index size N, implicit in the notation X_1,...,X_N and max_i. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, Exercise 2.6.5 opening and definition of K.]
Real-valued random variables X_1,...,X_N. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, Exercise 2.6.5; real coefficients a in R^N and the displayed real L^p inequality.]
A coefficient vector a=(a_1,...,a_N) in R^N. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, Exercise 2.6.5.]
A finite real exponent p with p in [2,infinity). [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, phrase 'for every p in [2, infinity)'.]
An absolute constant C>0, understood as universal rather than depending on N, the variables, a, or p. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, final phrase 'C is an absolute constant'.]
hypotheses: The random variables X_1,...,X_N are mutually independent. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, Exercise 2.6.5 opening sentence.]
Each X_i is sub-gaussian. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, Exercise 2.6.5 opening sentence; PDF page 16 / printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6.]
Each X_i has zero mean, E X_i=0. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, phrase 'with zero means'.]
Each X_i has unit variance, Var(X_i)=1. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, phrase 'unit variances'.]
The coefficient vector a is arbitrary in R^N, including possible zero coefficients. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, unqualified binder a in R^N.]
The exponent satisfies 2<=p<infinity. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, p in [2,infinity).]
conclusions: The Euclidean coefficient size is a lower bound for the L^p norm of the weighted sum: (sum_{i=1}^N a_i^2)^(1/2) <= ||sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i||_{L^p}. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, left half of the displayed inequality in Exercise 2.6.5.]

The L^p norm of the weighted sum is bounded above by the sub-gaussian Khintchine scale: ||sum_{i=1}^N a_i X_i||_{L^p} <= C K sqrt(p) (sum_{i=1}^N a_i^2)^(1/2). [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, right half of the displayed inequality in Exercise 2.6.5.]
Here K is exactly max_{1<=i<=N} ||X_i||_{psi_2}, and C is an absolute constant. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, sentence immediately following the display.]
definitions_and_conventions: The L^p norm convention is ||Z||_{L^p}=(E|Z|^p)^(1/p). [Source: PDF page 13 / printed page 24, Exercise 2.5.1 first display.]
The sub-gaussian norm is ||X||_{psi_2}=inf{t>0 : E exp(X^2/t^2)<=2}. [Source: PDF page 16 / printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and Equation (2.13).]
K abbreviates the maximum psi_2 norm of the finite family: K=max_{1<=i<=N} ||X_i||_{psi_2}. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, sentence following Exercise 2.6.5's display.]

The expression (sum_i a_i^2)^(1/2) is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, the same expression on both sides of the displayed inequality, with a declared in R^N.]

Equation (2.15) supplies the general moment-growth convention ||X||_{L^p} <= C ||X||_{psi_2} sqrt(p) for all p>=1, with an absolute constant. [Source: PDF page 16 / printed page 27, Equation (2.15) and its surrounding text.]
implicit_context: All X_i live on a common probability space so that independence and the sum sum_i a_i X_i are defined; the space is not named in the exercise. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, joint independence and weighted-sum notation.]

N is intended to be a positive integer: the source writes a finite family X_1,...,X_N and uses max_i, but does not separately quantify N>=1. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, opening sentence and definition of K.]

The absolute constant C is uniform across all admissible choices, following the book's explicit 'absolute constant' convention. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, final clause; PDF page 16 / printed page 27, text after equations (2.14)--(2.16).]
Sub-gaussianity ensures the finite moments required by the displayed L^p norm; Equation (2.15) explicitly provides them for p>=1. [Source: PDF page 16 / printed page 27, Equation (2.15).]

details: The claim is uniform over every finite independent family satisfying the stated distributional hypotheses, every real coefficient vector, and every p>=2. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, full Exercise 2.6.5 statement.]
C is absolute and K carries the family-specific sub-gaussian scale. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, sentence after the display.]
The exercise asks for both the lower Euclidean-energy bound and the upper sub-gaussian moment bound in one inequality chain. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, displayed inequality.]
The lower bound has constant exactly 1; only the upper bound contains C and K sqrt(p). [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, displayed inequality.]
Independence, zero mean, unit variance, and sub-gaussianity are all explicit assumptions and apply to every X_i. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, opening sentence.]
The asserted comparison is for every finite real p in [2,infinity), not merely integer p. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, explicit p-domain.]
The cited moment characterization (2.15) is stated on the wider range p>=1. [Source: PDF page 16 / printed page 27, Equation (2.15).]
Coefficients are arbitrary real numbers; no normalization or nonzero-energy condition is stated. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, a in R^N without qualification.]
Every sum and maximum is over i=1,...,N. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, displayed summation bounds and finite-family notation.]

undebatable_constraints: The formal claim must retain all four family hypotheses: independence, sub-gaussianity, zero means, and unit variances. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, Exercise 2.6.5 opening.]
It must quantify arbitrary real coefficients a in R^N and every finite real p>=2. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30.]
It must state both sides of the displayed comparison, with lower-bound constant exactly 1. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, displayed inequality.]
The upper bound must scale as C*K*sqrt(p)*(sum_i a_i^2)^(1/2). [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, displayed inequality.]
K must be the maximum of the individual psi_2 norms, not a sum, average, or unrelated bound. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, definition of K.]
C must be an absolute universal constant rather than data-dependent. [Source: PDF page 19 / printed page 30, final phrase.]

ambiguities.issue: The exercise does not explicitly quantify N or say N>=1.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 19 / printed page 30 writes X_1,...,X_N and K=max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2} without a separate N-binder.
ambiguities.impact: A formal target must choose a finite nonempty indexing representation; the maximum makes the empty-family case outside the literal notation unless separately totalized.

ambiguities.issue: The numerical value and explicit quantifier placement of C are not given.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 19 / printed page 30 says only 'C is an absolute constant'.
ambiguities.impact: A formal target should express existence of one positive universal C outside the family, coefficient, and exponent quantifiers, but cannot require a source-specified numerical value.

ambiguities.issue: The common probability space and measurability/integrability side conditions are left implicit.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 19 / printed page 30 uses random variables, expectations, variances, independence, and an L^p norm without naming the probability space or technical measurability hypotheses.
ambiguities.impact: Lean may expose these standard well-formedness conditions explicitly; doing so should not change the mathematical family covered.

contract_plain_english: There is a universal absolute constant C such that, for every positive finite family of independent real sub-gaussian random variables with mean zero and variance one, every real coefficient vector a, and every finite real p>=2, the L^p norm of the weighted sum lies between the Euclidean norm of a and C times the largest psi_2 norm in the family times sqrt(p) times that Euclidean norm. The source imposes no normalization or nonzero condition on a.
